reason: Brakes on sprouting angiogenesis (G4/G5) and vessel repair and remodeling (G2) are core; smooth-muscle remodeling (G1) and clotting/ECM turnover (G3) are other parts of wound repair.
Purine catabolism and salvage via ADA/PNP (G1/G3) is the core; nucleoside transport and NTP breakdown (G2) cover the extracellular supply and handling of adenosine.
Facilitation is a presynaptic, calcium-dependent increase in release probability, which all fitting groups describe; inhibitory synapse assembly (G4) does not fit.
CTLA4 is a co-inhibitor that opposes CD28 costimulation and TCR signaling, so all three groups are the same T-cell co-signaling axis.
Cardiac membrane potential and SR calcium release (G1) is the core, and the groups on rate, force and SR calcium uptake (G2/G3) are the same excitation-contraction coupling.
Regulation of clathrin-independent and raft endocytosis (G3/G4) is the core; muscle membrane/T-tubule raft biology (G2) and cholesterol handling (G5) are other caveolar roles.
All three groups are about neurotrophin TRK receptor activation and its RAS/PI3K/PLCG downstream signaling, centred on NTRK2.
The groups show different parts of the HCMV life cycle: latency and early-stage control, ESCRT-mediated virion egress, and nuclear-pore traffic of the viral genome.
Upstream AKT and acetylation control of FOXO (G2) differs from FOXO's metabolic fasting output with PGC1a and gluconeogenesis (G3) and from its loose beta-cell and circadian context (G1).
All groups hold the paralogous FGFR downstream cascades (PI3K, FRS, SHC, PLC), which is the same signaling module the target belongs to.
Bacterial entry into host cells (G3/G4) is the core; E-cadherin trafficking and degradation (G1) and actin-driven uptake (G2) are host-mechanism sides of InlA entry.
ATF4 appears as one transcriptional arm of the ER UPR (G1/G3), as the effector of eIF2a-driven translation control and the integrated stress response (G2/G5), and in beta-cell ER-stress death (G4).

Oxidative-stress responses and cell death (G1) are the core; ROS generation (G4) and alveolar epithelium/surfactant biology (G5) are the lung-injury context; general organogenesis and mammary groups do not fit.
Connexin trafficking and gap junction biogenesis (G3) differs from the cardiac electrical coupling and conduction that gap junctions serve (G2) and from conduction-system development (G1).
Cell-cycle machinery and checkpoints (G1/G2/G4) differ from the AKT/TSC/mTOR survival and growth arm (G3) that the module also contains.

Dual-specificity phosphatase inactivation of MAPKs (G1/G3) is the core; CDK/Cdc25 cell-cycle control (G2) and AKT/PTEN regulation (G5) are other phospho-threonine switches; inositol-phosphate metabolism (G4) does not fit.
Monoamine and serotonin degradation (G1/G2) is the core; flavin-dependent amine oxidation and its inherited defect FMO3/TMAU (G3) is a loosely related metabolic-disease side.
Smooth muscle contraction and adrenergic control (G2/G3) is the mechanism, while parturition and reproductive physiology (G1) is the organismal context.
The fitting groups are sensorimotor coordination of posture, righting and locomotion, which is the same proprioceptive function; MECP2 gene regulation (G4) does not fit.
Nucleic-acid sensing via RIG-I, TLR and STING that triggers DC cytokines (G2-G5) differs from the Th1-polarizing cytokine output of DCs (G1).
